subtitle: B2 · Unit 10: B2 · Community debate: connect ideas without losing the thread

steps.title: Reference and cohesion: use en and y only when the link is clear
steps.body: En can replace a previously named complement introduced by de (parler des horaires → en parler); y can replace a place or a complement introduced by à (revenir à la proposition → y revenir). They help avoid repetition, but a pronoun is useful only when the listener can identify its reference. In a multi-speaker summary, repeat the key noun if en or y could refer to two different ideas. Use lexical links (ce point, cette mesure, la proposition) to keep the thread visible. Agreement and meaning still depend on the full sentence.

steps.title: Reference and cohesion: use en and y only when the link is clear
rows: Les horaires? Nous en parlerons à la prochaine rencontre.
The schedule? We will talk about it at the next meeting.
La proposition est complexe; nous y reviendrons.
The proposal is complex; we will return to it.
La salle reste accessible; cette priorité est partagée.
The room remains accessible; this priority is shared.
Mina propose une soirée parce que plusieurs personnes travaillent le jour.
Mina proposes an evening because several people work during the day.

steps.prompt: In Nous en parlerons, what does en replace?
steps.explain: En often replaces a complement introduced by de.

steps.prompt: In Nous y reviendrons, what does y refer to?
steps.explain: Y can replace a place or an à-complement.

steps.prompt: When should you repeat a noun?
options: When the pronoun's reference could be unclear
steps.explain: Repeating the noun can prevent ambiguity.
